models_evaluated: Institution-specific L2-regularized logistic regression CDI Risk Score

links.outcome: CDI incidence and CDI-associated antimicrobial use before vs after AI deployment
links.effect: Despite AUROC 0.822, no significant CDI reduction (5.76 vs 5.65 per 10 000 patient-days; P = .85); piperacillin-tazobactam use fell −9.64 days/1000 (P < .001), clindamycin −1.04 (P = .03).
links.quote: Although we did not observe a significant reduction in CDI incidence, we observed significant reductions in the use of CDI-associated antimicrobials.

links.outcome: Pharmacist engagement with AI high-risk flag in existing review dashboard
links.effect: Flag used to sort pharmacist medication review queue; 6 of 7 pharmacists found workflow not disruptive, all 7 contacted care teams; piperacillin-tazobactam relative reduction 16.8% in high-risk alerted patients.
links.quote: However, of the 7 pharmacists interviewed, 6 indicated the new workflow was not disruptive, and all 7 contacted the patients’ care team based on the alerts (eTables 7 and 8 in Supplement 1 ).

links.outcome: Adherence to bundle components by workflow fit
links.effect: Components integrated into existing pharmacist workflows were used and reduced antimicrobial use; multistage new-behavior hand hygiene component had low adherence and failed.
links.quote: In contrast, our efforts had the greatest association with antimicrobial stewardship, likely because the AI guidance was integrated into current workflows of pharmacists.

links.outcome: Clinician response to AI-triggered best practice advisory alerts
links.effect: Of 17 practitioners interviewed, 6 tended to ignore the BPAs and 10 could not recall BPA content, despite only 1-2 study BPAs per week.
links.quote: Of the 17 primary inpatient practitioners interviewed, 6 indicated that they tended to ignore the BPAs and 10 could not recall the BPA content.

models_evaluated: CDI Risk Score: institution-specific L2-regularized logistic regression with time-varying parameters

links.outcome: CDI incidence and CDI-associated antimicrobial use after AI-guided prevention
links.effect: CDI incidence: 5.76 vs 5.65 per 10 000 patient-days; absolute difference, −0.11; 95% CI, −1.43 to 1.18; P = .85. CDI-associated antimicrobial use decreased.
links.quote: In this quality improvement study, the implementation of an AI-guided infection prevention bundle was not associated with a significant reduction in the already low CDI incidence rate at the study site, but it was associated with reduced CDI-associated antimicrobial use.

links.outcome: Antimicrobial use following AI-prioritized medication reviews within a multicomponent prevention bundle
links.effect: With the bundle including prioritized medication reviews, high-risk hospitalizations had a piperacillin-tazobactam relative reduction of 16.8% [95% CI, 8.0%-24.6%; P < .001], versus no significant change in low-risk hospitalizations.
links.quote: Reductions were more prominent in high-risk hospitalizations alerted by the AI tool (eg, piperacillin-tazobactam: relative reduction of 16.8% [95% CI, 8.0%-24.6%; P < .001] in high risk vs no significant change in low risk) (eTables 5 and 6 in Supplement 1 ).

links.outcome: Practitioner engagement with AI-triggered best practice advisories
links.effect: Of 17 primary inpatient practitioners interviewed, 6 tended to ignore the BPAs and 10 could not recall their content; field observations also found low adherence to enhanced hand hygiene.
links.quote: Of the 17 primary inpatient practitioners interviewed, 6 indicated that they tended to ignore the BPAs and 10 could not recall the BPA content.

models_evaluated: institution-specific L2-regularized logistic regression CDI risk model

links.effect: No significant reduction in CDI incidence (absolute difference, -0.11 per 10,000 patient-days).
links.quote: After adjusting for differences in clinical characteristics, there was no significant reduction in CDI incidence (pre-AI period: 5.76 per 10 000 patient-days vs post-AI period: 5.65 per 10 000 patient-days; absolute difference, -0.11; 95% CI, -1.43 to 1.18; P = .85).

links.effect: Multistage workflow requirements led to BPAs being ignored, hand hygiene orders not created, and signs not followed.
links.quote: This multistage behavior change created a so-called leaky pipeline: BPAs were often ignored, and orders for enhanced hand hygiene were not created; even when orders were placed, the signs were not always posted or followed.

links.effect: Relative reductions greater than 10% in normalized antimicrobial days for piperacillin-tazobactam (-9.64) and clindamycin (-1.04).
links.quote: Relative reductions greater than 10% in normalized antimicrobial days were seen for piperacillin-tazobactam (-9.64; 95% CI, -12.93 to -6.28; P < .001) and clindamycin (-1.04; 95% CI, -1.60 to -0.47; P = .03), especially for high-risk patients alerted by AI (relative reduction for piperacillin-tazobactam, 16.8%; 95% CI, 8.0%-24.6%).
